title: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yitzchak
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Sukkah 44b: Aivu said (Rav’s father, according to Rashi): “I was standing before Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yitzchak (according to Dikdukei Soferim’s reading). A man came before him and asked him about a law of the Sabbatical year.” Aivu also said in his name there that a person should not walk more than three parasangs on the eve of Shabbat.
This reading was also before Yuchasin, and Hyman considers Seder HaDorot’s criticism needless under the entry Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok.

notes.text: שאל יהלך is ש + אל יהלך: that one should NOT walk more than three parasangs on Shabbat eve, not a question asking permission. The supplied דר״א lacks an explicit קמיה, supplied as “before.” Saved Davidson Sukkah 44b writes Elazar bar Tzadok for the prohibition; Hyman’s Dikdukei Soferim Yitzchak reading and criticism remain distinct.

The consulted Sukkah 44b prohibition names Elazar bar Tzadok. Hyman’s Yitzchak reading in Dikdukei Soferim and his account of Yuchasin remain edition claims whose exact printed witnesses have not been independently inspected.
